tip: Спасибо, что (spasibo, chto) plus a past-tense verb means thanks for doing something: написал (napisal = wrote).
Хорошо, что (khorosho, chto = good that) opens a clause giving the reason you are glad: ты позвонил (ty pozvonil = you called).
накопила денег (nakopila deneg) puts деньги (dengi = money) into genitive to mean saved some money, an unspecified amount, not a named sum.
Paired Или... или (ili... ili = either... or) marks the two choices: идём (idyom = we go) or остаёмся (ostayomsya = we stay).
After Нет (net = there is no) the noun goes genitive: сомнений (somneniy = doubts), never nominative сомнения (somneniya).
домой (domoy = homeward) is the motion form for heading home; дома (doma) would mean being at home with no movement.
так... что (tak... chto = so... that) ties a degree to its result: так быстро (tak bystro = so fast) that понять (ponyat) is hard.
Для того чтобы (dlya togo chtoby = in order to) plus an infinitive states purpose: получить (poluchit = to get) a visa.
успеть на (uspet na) takes accusative and means make it in time for: успели на поезд (uspeli na poezd = made the train).
Дело в том, что (delo v tom, chto = the thing is that) is a fixed frame for introducing the real explanation.
Unreal past conditions use Если бы (esli by) plus a past verb, then бы (by) again in the result: знал (znal = knew), пришёл (prishyol = came).
Давай (davay) plus a perfective we-form makes a suggestion: Давай сходим (davay skhodim = let us go).
Желаю (zhelayu = I wish) takes the genitive of what you wish: приятного вечера (priyatnogo vechera = a pleasant evening).
Едва... как (edva... kak = barely... when) links one action to the next that follows right after: закончил (zakonchil = finished), then раздался (razdalsya = rang).
Вместо того чтобы (vmesto togo chtoby = instead of) plus an infinitive: учиться (uchitsya = to study) rather than doing something else.
Paired Ни... ни (ni... ni = neither... nor) still keeps не on the verb: не знали (ne znali = did not know).
В то время как (v to vremya kak = while) plus imperfectives shows two actions running at once: работал (rabotal), готовила (gotovila).
The -ся (-sya) ending makes соблюдается (soblyudaetsya = is observed) passive: the tradition gets kept, with no actor named.
Кто бы ни (kto by ni = whoever) plus a past verb means no matter who: пришёл (prishyol = came), everyone was glad.
